open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct and formally verify a terminating exact procedure on finite rational-semialgebraic covariance-region codes that realizes \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\), certifies release or abstention, classifies \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) as empty, singleton, or multiple, and computes a certified positive lower bound for the far-family residual and hence an effective \(r_0>0\); also verify normalization-chart changes and a corruption-aware \(\texttt{backShift}\) implementation.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core defines \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) only set-theoretically for arbitrary nonempty covariance regions. Moreover, \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\) assumes a feasibility oracle returning full solution sets and expressly supplies no terminating solver, while \(\text{thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction}\) obtains \(r_0\) non-effectively from compactness and a positive far-family residual. The core contains no finite coding syntax and semantics, quantifier-elimination, sign-determination, or root-isolation algorithm with termination and exactness proofs; no constructive lower bound for that residual; no decision theorem for the declarative universal candidate condition-number premise; and no formal specification of chart transformations or the CRAN workflow. Consequently the requested executable, effective, and software claims do not follow from the declared primitives or established results.
open_obligations.attempted: Reuse of \(\text{thm:confidence-union-coverage}\) and \(\text{thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction}\) closes the mathematical coverage and local-contraction components. Composing them with \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\) does not close the residual: the latter is an oracle reduction, not an implementation, and the compactness proof provides existence but neither a computable modulus nor a terminating certificate. No honest narrowing answers the requested combined executable program without adding and proving a new formal real-algebraic and software-verification substrate.
